name: centipede
about: Chain ragdoll body for the giant centipede (Armagedom 75-bone roach rig: ONE rigid body bone, 11 leg pairs, no spine). The rig has no segment bones, so the chain is laid on synthetic points along the body's long axis (data/bodies/centipede.bones.json axis_*): 6 body segments seg1..seg6 (seg3 is the root, it starts at the body bone), a head, and one leg bank per side per segment (12 banks, ball joint to the segment). Each bank is the first leg of its group (root to foot) and carries the group's other legs as followers. Which model bones move: seg3 drives the 'body' bone (every bone not listed below hangs off it), seg2 drives 'thorax', seg5 drives 'abdomen', the head drives 'head', each bank drives one leg bone and the follow list names the rest of its group; seg1, seg4 and seg6 are VIRTUAL (drives null): they are simulated and carry the banks, but no model bone moves for them. Shins and feet are children of their leg bone and ride it. Every number is here; src/chain.mjs holds none.
placeholder_note: radii, masses, joint limits, the segment boundaries (0.06 model units apart, chosen so every leg pair lies under exactly one segment) and the rear stub are PLACEHOLDERS to tune on Dom's phone and the clips; only the bone positions are measured. The visible bend is limited to what the rig can show: the game can only rotate bones (three-rig sets position for the root and cut bones only), so the body skin bends at thorax / body / abdomen and the legs swing about their own roots.
scale_source: Armagedom Web/src/data/creatureDefinitions.json giant-centipede scale.model = 3 (character 1.265 and visual 1.3225 are applied by the actor wrapper on top and are NOT in this scale, the same choice as the salamander's 3.6). Bones and radii below are in model units (the GLB's armature node scale 0.6 is already in the bone positions), the row is in metres at this scale.
mass_assumption: placeholder: about 1.3 m long and 0.4 m across at x3; 21 kg total is a light estimate for a flat-bodied arthropod that size (body segments 2.5 each, head 1.5, leg banks 0.4 each). Tune against how heavy the fall should feel.
